region $ \sqrt[3]{2}<q<Q_{0}$ where $P_{s}<0$ is an unphysical negative-cost
tail of the log.  The economically relevant producer surplus is therefore

$PS_{e}= \int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-P_{s}(q)\big]dq
      =P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}
        \ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq$,

and not $P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}$.  With $Q_{0}\approx1.442$,

$\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx 9.8\!-\!10.0$,

$P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})\approx 4.62\,(4.69-1.44)\approx14.9\!-\!15.0$,

hence

$PS_{e}\approx14.98-9.90\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$,

about $5.1$ on the Simpson grid used above.  The usual textbook total
surplus is then

$W_{e}=CS+PS_{e}
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq-P^{*}Q_{0}
      -\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq$,

i.e. the willingness to pay up to $Q^{*}$ minus the variable cost
incurred from the zero-price point onward.  Numerically

$W_{e}\approx 32.45-4.62\times1.442-9.90
   \approx 32.45-6.66-9.90
   \approx 15.9$,

$CS\approx10.8$, $PS_{e}\approx5.1$, $W_{e}\approx15\!-\!16$ monetary
units at $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.

The often quoted $\approx22\!-\!23$ “area between the curves’’
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}dq\approx32.5-9.9\approx
22.6$ is the gross net benefit $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}$
and contains the $P^{*}Q_{0}$ rectangle.  Removing that rectangle, which
is the usual $CS+PS$ definition with $PS$ measured from the zero-price
intercept, gives the economically meaningful total welfare $\approx15.9\approx
16$ at the competitive equilibrium $Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.6$. ∎

17.text:
The market clears for $Q_{S}=Q_{D}=Q^{*}$ on

$$P_{S}(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right), \qquad 
P_{D}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q},\qquad  Q>2^{1/3},$$

i.e.

$$F(Q):=\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0 .
$$

$F$ is strictly increasing from $-\infty$ to $+\infty$ on the admissible
branch and $F(4.5)<0<F(4.7)$.  Newton / bisection gives the unique interior
root

$$Q^{*}\approx 4.68\!-\!4.72\approx 4.69 ,\qquad 
t^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36\;{\rm rad},$$

$$P^{*}=P_{S}(Q^{*})=P_{D}(Q^{*})
     =\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.61\!-\!4.63
     \approx4.62,
$$

and $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 21.6\!-\!21.8$.

Put $D(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ and $S(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)$.  With the usual
surplus definitions

\[
CS(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad 
PS(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq,
\]

\[
W(Q^{*})=CS+PS=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-\int_{Q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq,
\]

$Q_{a}=2^{1/3}$ being the formal domain of the log supply.  On the
regularised part

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
          =18\int_{0}^{t^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt\approx 3.24\!-\!3.28\times10^{1}
          \approx32.5,$$

\[
I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})=\int_{a}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
               \approx9.6\!-\!9.8 .
\]

Hence on the gross area–between–the–curves convention

\[
CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0\approx10.8,
\]

\[
PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.7\approx11.8\!-\!12.0,
\]

and

\[
W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}
       =I_{D}(Q^{*})-I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})\approx32.5-9.9\approx22\!-\!23,
\]

e.g. $W_{g}^{*}\approx22.6$ for $Q^{*}\!\approx\!4.69$, $P^{*}\!\approx\!4.62$.
This is the $ \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-\int_{a}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$ ‘area between the
curves’ normally quoted, $CS^{*}\approx\$10.8$, $PS_{g}^{*}\approx\$11.8$,
$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx\$21.7$ at the competitive pair $Q^{*}\!\approx\!4.7$,
$P^{*}\!\approx\!4.6$.

*Remark on the zero-price normalisation.*  $S(Q)\ge0$ for $Q\ge Q_{0}$,
$Q_{0}^{3}=3$, $Q_{0}= \root3\of3\approx1.442$.  With the economically
relevant lower limit

\[
J(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq\approx9.8\!-\!10.0,
\]

\[
PS_{e}^{*}=P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-J(Q^{*})\approx5.0\!-\!5.3\approx5.1,
\]

\[
W_{e}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{e}^{*}
       =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-J(Q^{*})\approx15\!-\!16\approx15.9,
\]

i.e. $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{e}^{*}\approx5.1$, $W_{e}^{*}\approx15.9$,
the $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.66$ rectangle being removed when the negative–price
tail $2^{1/3}<q<\root3\of3$ of the log supply is discarded.  $W_{e}^{*}=W_{g}^{*}
-P^{*}Q_{0}$ is the conventional zero-price producer surplus version.

16.text:
The clearing price is the unique solution of

$$P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\iff 
\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv P(Q) ,
\qquad Q>2^{1/3},$$

$P_{S}$ increasing from $-\infty$ and $P_{D}$ decreasing from $18$ to
$18e^{-\pi/2}$.  Numerically

* $f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$,
* $f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$,

so that to the usual Newton tolerance

$$
Q^{*}\simeq4.69\!-\!4.70\approx4.69 ,\qquad 
t^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\simeq1.36\;{\rm rad},
$$

$$
P^{*}= \ln\big(Q^{*3}-2\big)=18e^{-t^{*}}
      \simeq4.61\!-\!4.63\approx4.62,
\qquad P^{*}Q^{*}\simeq21.6\!-\!21.8 .
$$

Put $D(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and $S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$.  With the textbook
inverse-surplus convention

$$
CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)\,dq-P^{*}Q^{*}, \qquad
PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)\,dq ,
$$

$Q_{0}$ the zero price of the inverse supply,
$S(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3$, $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$, and

$$
W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)\,dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)\,dq
     =I_{D}(Q^{*})-J(Q^{*}),
$$

is the finite area between demand and marginal supply up to $Q^{*}$.

With $u=\arctan q$, $dq=\sec^{2}u\,du$,

$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})=18\int_{0}^{t^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du
           =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx 3.24\!-\!3.26\times10^{1}
$$

$\approx32.4\!-\!32.6$, and

$$
J(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\big(q^{3}-2\big)dq\approx9.8\!-\!10.1,
$$

e.g. $I_{D}\approx32.46$ and $J\approx9.9$ on the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
$P^{*}\approx4.62$ root.  Hence in the usual gross normalisation

$$
CS^{*}=I_{D}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0\approx10.8,
$$

$$
PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-J\approx21.7-9.9\approx11.8\!-\!12.0,
$$

and

$$
W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}=I_{D}-J\approx32.5-9.9\approx
2.2\!-\!2.4\times10^{1}\approx22\!-\!23,
$$

about $W_{g}^{*}\simeq22.5\!-\!22.8$, e.g. $W_{g}^{*}\approx22.6$ with
$Q^{*}=4.692$, $P^{*}=4.62$, $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{g}^{*}\approx11.8$,
$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$.  This is the $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-
\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$ area normally quoted as $CS+PS$.

If producer surplus is measured from the economic zero-price intercept,
$PS_{e}=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}[P^{*}-S(q)]dq
      =P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-J$,

$$
PS_{e}\approx P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-J\approx14.9-9.9\approx5.0\!-\!5.3\approx5.1,
$$

and the net economically relevant surplus

$$
W_{e}=CS^{*}+PS_{e}=I_{D}-P^{*}Q_{0}-J\approx32.5-6.66-9.9\approx15\!-\!17,
$$

typically $W_{e}\approx15.9\approx16$, $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{e}\approx5.1$,
the $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.6$ rectangle being the difference between the
gross $W_{g}^{*}\approx22\!-\!23$ and the net $W_{e}\approx15\!-\!16$
convention.  The equilibrium $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ is
stable under all quadratures. ∎

10.text:
In a competitive inverse set-up
$P_{S}(Q)=\ln (Q^{3}-2),\;Q>2^{1/3}$ , $P_{D}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$
the clearing pair is the unique solution of

$$F(Q)=\ln (Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln \!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\;,$$

$F'>0$ on $Q>2^{1/3}$ and $F(4.5)<0<F(4.7)$.  Newton/bisection gives

* $Q^{*}\simeq 4.68\!-\!4.71$,  $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
* $P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.61\!-\!4.63$,
  $P^{*}\approx4.62$,   $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.6\!-\!21.8$,

the usual $Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.6$ competitive point.
Put $D(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ and $S(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)$.  On the textbook
surplus convention

$$CS(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad
PS(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq ,$$

with the zero–price intercept of the inverse supply
$S(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3$, $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$.
Writing $I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D$ and $I_{S}(Q^{*})=
\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S$,

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx 32.4\!-\!32.8
\approx 32.5, $$

$$I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
\approx 9.8\!-\!10.1\approx 9.9, $$

so that in the usual $P^{*}Q^{*}$ normalisation

$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0
\approx10.8$,

$PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.9\approx11.8$,

and the area between demand and marginal supply up to the clearing
quantity

$$W^{*} = CS^{*}+PS^{*}
      =I_{D}(Q^{*})-I_{S}(Q^{*})
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
      \approx 32.5-9.9\approx 2.2\!-\!2.4\times10^{1},$$

about $W^{*}\simeq22\!-\!23$, $W^{*}\approx22.6$ with the
$Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ numerical root, $CS^{*}\approx
\$10.8$ and $PS^{*}\approx\$11.8$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx\$21.7$.  This is the
finite $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}[P_{D}-P_{S}]dq$ surplus normally quoted in the
literature for the model.

Remark on the economic origin.  $S(Q)<0$ for
$2^{1/3}<Q<3^{1/3}$.  Removing the negative–price tail and defining
producer surplus strictly as $\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}[P^{*}-S(q)]dq$ gives
the economically non–negative
$PS_{e}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-I_{S}(Q^{*})\approx5.0\!-\!5.3\approx5.1$ and

$$W_{e}=CS^{*}+PS_{e}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-I_{S}(Q^{*})
      \approx32.5-6.66-9.9\approx15\!-\!16\approx15.9, $$

i.e. $CS\approx10.8$, $PS_{e}\approx5.1$, $W_{e}\approx15.9$, the
$P^{*}Q_{0}$ rectangle being removed from the gross $22\!-\!23$ figure.
The $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ clearing pair is the same in
either convention. ∎

14.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The clearing price is indeed the unique solution of
$\ln(Q^{3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ on $Q>2^{1/3}$.
$F(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$ is monotone increasing and
$F(4.68)<0<F(4.70)$, Newton gives

$Q^{*}\simeq4.69\!-\!4.70$, $t^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\simeq1.36$,
$P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-t^{*}}\simeq4.61\!-\!4.63$, 
say $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$.

With $P_{d}(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$,
$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq$,
$I_{D}(Q^{*})=18\int_{0}^{t^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt\approx 32.4\!-\!32.5$,
so that on the usual definition

$CS= I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!10.9$,
about $10.8$ in the same units.

The inverse marginal cost $P_{s}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ is negative on
$2^{1/3}<q<3^{1/3}$.  The economic origin of supply is $P_{s}=0$,
$P_{s}(q_{0})=0\iff q_{0}^{3}=3$,

$q_{0}=\root3\of{3}\approx1.44$, and $P_{s}(q)\ge0$ for $q\ge q_{0}$.
The economically meaningful producer surplus is therefore

$PS =\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[\,P^{*}-P_{s}(q)\,\big]dq
    =P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-q_{0}\right)-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$.

Numerically
$J(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8\!-\!10.0$,
$P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_{0})\approx4.62\,(4.69-1.44)\approx14.9\!-\!15.0$,
hence

$PS\approx14.98-9.86\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$, about $5.1$.

Hence the dead-weight-free surplus measured from the zero-price
origin is

$W_{e}=CS+PS
      =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_{0}-J(Q^{*})
      \approx32.5-4.62\times1.44-9.9\approx15\!-\!16$,

e.g. $I_{D}\approx32.4$, $P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.65$, $J\approx9.86$ giving
$W_{e}\approx15.9$.  In particular $CS\approx10.8$ and $PS_{e}\approx5.1$
for $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.

The formal “area between the curves’’ 
$W_{b}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-J(Q^{*})\approx32.5-9.9\approx22.6$,
$CS+PS+P^{*}q_{0}$, is often quoted as the gross $P_{d}-P_{s}$ area.
Removing the non-economic $P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.6$ rectangle that arises
from integrating the log supply through its negative-price region
$2^{1/3}<q<3^{1/3}$ leaves the $ \sim15\!-\!16$ net consumer-plus-producer
surplus that is normally used in welfare accounting. ∎

public_text.4:
The inverse market is

$P_{S}(Q)=\ln \left(Q^{3}-2\right)$, $\;Q>2^{1/3}$, 
$P_{D}(Q)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}$,

and the competitive clearing point is the unique solution of

$\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv P^{*}$,
$Q>2^{1/3}$.

$L(Q)=\ln (Q^{3}-2)$ is strictly increasing from $-\infty$ to $+\infty$
and $R(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ is strictly decreasing from $18$ to
$18e^{-\pi/2}\approx3.74$, so the root is unique.  Newton / bisection

$f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$,
$f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$

gives

$Q^{*}\approx 4.68\!-\!4.70\approx4.69$,
$t^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36$ rad,

$P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-t^{*}}\approx4.61\!-\!4.63$,
$P^{*}\approx4.62$,
$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.6\!-\!21.8$.

Put $I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq
      =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq$.
With $u=\arctan q$, $dq=\sec^{2}u\,du$,

$I_{D}(Q^{*})=18\int_{0}^{t^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du\approx 32.4\!-\!32.8$,
about $32.5$ on the usual Simpson grids.

The inverse supply is negative on $2^{1/3}<q<3^{1/3}$.  With the
conventional zero price normalisation

$P_{S}(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}-2=1\iff Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.44$,

$J(Q^{*})=\displaystyle\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
      \approx9.6\!-\!10.1\approx9.9$

is the finite variable-cost area.  Then in the textbook
consumer-plus-producer surplus convention

$CS^{*}=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*}$,
$PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq$,

$CS^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0\approx10.8$,
$PS_{g}^{*}\approx21.7-9.9\approx11.8\!-\!12.0$,

and the gross area between the demand curve and the marginal supply
curve up to the competitive quantity

$W_{b}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}
       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
       \approx32.5-9.9\approx22\!-\!23$,

about $W_{b}^{*}\approx22.6$ with $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$,
i.e. $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{g}^{*}\approx11.8$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$.

Remark on the economic normalisation.  If producer surplus is measured
from the zero price origin, $PS_{e}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-J(Q^{*})\approx
5.0\!-\!5.3$, the economically trimmed total surplus is

$W_{e}=CS^{*}+PS_{e}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-J(Q^{*})\approx15\!-\!16$,
$\approx15.9$ with the numbers above, the $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.66$
rectangle being removed.  The $W_{b}^{*}\approx22\!-\!23$ quoted above is
the usual textbook $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$
area at the competitive equilibrium $Q^{*}\simeq4.7$, $P^{*}\simeq4.6$.

$P_{S}(Q^{*})=P_{D}(Q^{*})$

$$

\qquad CS^{*}\approx10.8 .$$

The supply integral on the regular part of the curve is

$$I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.6\!-\!10.0, $$

about $9.7\!-\!9.9$ on the zero-price part $q\ge q_{0}^{p}=3^{1/3}$.
Hence the gross producer surplus on the formal domain

$$PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.7\approx11.8\!-\!12.0, $$

and the gross area between the curves up to the competitive quantity

$$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
      =I_{D}(Q^{*})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[D(q)-S(q)\big]dq\approx22\!-\!24, $$

about

$$W^{*}\approx32.5-9.9\approx22.6, $$

i.e. $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS^{*}\approx11.8$ and $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$
for $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.

Remark on the zero-price normalisation.  $S(q)<0$ for
$2^{1/3}<q<3^{1/3}$ and $S(q_{0}^{p})=0$ with $q_{0}^{p}=3^{1/3}\approx1.44$.
With the economically meaningful truncation

$$PS_{e}= \int_{q_{0}^{p}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-S(q)\big]dq
      =P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-q_{0}^{p}\right)-\int_{q_{0}^{p}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
      \approx5.0\!-\!5.3, $$

$$W_{e}=CS^{*}+PS_{e}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_{0}^{p}
       -\int_{q_{0}^{p}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq\approx15\!-\!17, $$

about $W_{e}\approx15.9$, $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{e}\approx5.1$, which is
the net surplus measured from the zero-price origin $q_{0}^{p}=3^{1/3}$.
The $ \approx 22\!-\!23$ number above is the conventional gross
$CS+PS$ area $\,I_{D}-I_{S}$ normally quoted for the model. ∎

The inverse market clears on

\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q}, \qquad Q>2^{1/3}, $$

and $R(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ is strictly decreasing from $18$ to
$18e^{-\pi/2}$.  The root is unique.  

$F(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$

* $F(4.68)<0$, $F(4.70)>0$,

Newton/bisection gives

$$Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.70\approx4.69 ,$$

$$P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}
      \approx4.61\!-\!4.63\approx4.62, $$

$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.6\!-\!21.8$.

Put $D(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and $S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$.  With the usual
textbook normalisation the zero–price intercept of the inverse supply is

$$S(q_{0})=0\iff q_{0}^{3}=3,\qquad q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.44, $$

and

$$CS^{*}=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad 
PS_{0}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq,
$$

so that the gross area between demand and marginal supply up to the
competitive quantity is

$$W_{0}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{0}^{*}
       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq .$$

Numerically

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
          \approx 3.24\!-\!3.30\times10^{1}\approx32.4\!-\!32.7,$$

$$I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8\!-\!10.0,$$

hence with the $Q^{*}\approx4.69,\;P^{*}\approx4.62$ root

* $CS^{*}=I_{D}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0\approx10.8$,
* $PS_{0}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}\approx21.7-9.9\approx11.8\!-\!12.0$,

and

$$W_{0}^{*}=I_{D}-I_{S}\approx32.5-9.9\approx22\!-\!23, $$

e.g. $W_{0}^{*}\approx22.6\!-\!23.0$ on Simpson/Newton quadrature,
$CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{0}^{*}\approx11.8$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$.

$$W_{0}(Q^{*})=18\!\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq

$PS_{e}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_{0})-I_{S}\approx5.0\!-\!5.3\approx5.1$ and

     =I_{D}-P^{*}q_{0}-I_{S}\approx32.5-6.66-9.9\approx15\!-\!16,
$$

Market clearing is

$$P_{S}(Q)=\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=P_{D}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}=P^{*},
\qquad Q>2^{1/3}, $$

$P_{S}$ increasing, $P_{D}$ decreasing.  $F(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$

* $F(4.68)<0$, $F(4.70)>0$,

so that with a Newton/bisection correction

\qquad

$$

is finite.  With $u=\arctan q$, $I_{D}=18\int_{0}^{t^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du$,

$$Q_{0}^{3}=3,\qquad Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.44, $$

and $a=2^{1/3}\approx1.26$ the formal domain of $\ln(Q^{3}-2)$.

$\approx15.9$ with the numbers above, $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{e}\approx5.1$,

public_text.8:
The equilibrium itself is settled. 
$P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)$ is
$\ln(Q^{3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$,

and

$CS=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*}$,

hence

$\displaystyle J(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8\!-\!10.0$,

and

$P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)\approx4.62\,(4.69-1.44)\approx14.9\!-\!15.0$,

$P_{s}(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}-2=1\iff Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$.

$W_{e}=CS+PS
     =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-J(Q^{*})
     \approx32.5-4.62\times1.442-9.9\approx15\!-\!17$,

           \approx32.5-9.9\approx22\!-\!23 ,$$

e.g. $W_{N}\approx22.6$ for $Q^{*}=4.69$, $P^{*}=4.62$, 
$CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{g}^{*}\approx11.8$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$.
With the formal domain $q_{m}=2^{1/3}$ the same integral is
$W_{N}\approx22.2\!-\!22.8$, the $\approx0.13$ negative-price tail
$\int_{q_{m}}^{q_{0}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$ being negligible.

Removing the $P^{*}q_{0}$ rectangle the economically quoted
producer surplus is

$$PS_{e}^{*}= \int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-P_{S}(q)\big]dq
          =P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-q_{0}\right)-J(Q^{*})\approx5.0\!-\!5.3,
$$

and the net welfare conventionally quoted as $CS+PS_{e}$

$$W_{e}=CS^{*}+PS_{e}^{*}
     =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_{0}-J(Q^{*})
     \approx32.5-6.66-9.9\approx15\!-\!16\approx15.9,$$

i.e. $CS\approx10.8$ and $PS_{e}\approx5.1$ on the zero-price
normalisation $q_{0}=3^{1/3}$.  The $22\!-\!23$ figure above is the
usual textbook $ \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$ gross
area between the curves at the competitive equilibrium
$Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.6$.  This is the $W^{*}\approx22.5$
normally reported; the $15\!-\!16$ net value is $W_{e}=W_{N}-P^{*}q_{0}$
with the conventional zero-price producer surplus. ∎
public_text.18:
The market clears on the interior branch $Q>2^{1/3}$ from

$$
P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\iff \ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv P(Q) ,
$$

LHS $\uparrow$, RHS $\downarrow$ so the root is unique.  
Numerically

* $f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$,
* $f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$,

$$
Q^{*}\approx4.69\!-\!4.70\approx4.69,\qquad 
t^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36\;{\rm rad},
$$

$$
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-t^{*}}\approx4.61\!-\!4.63\approx4.62,
$$

$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 4.62\times4.69\approx21.6\!-\!21.8$.

With the usual inverse-surplus definitions

$$
CS(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad 
I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq ,
$$

$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})=18\int_{0}^{t^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt\approx 32.4\!-\!32.8
$$

so that on the equilibrium quoted above

$$
CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0\approx10.8,
$$

essentially independent of the supply integration convention.

Let $Q_{0}^{p}$ be the economic zero of inverse supply,
$P_{S}(Q_{0}^{p})=0\iff Q_{0}^{p}=\root3\of3\approx1.44$, and
$Q_{m}= \root3\of2\approx1.26$ the formal domain of $\ln(Q^{3}-2)$.  On
the non-negative part

$$
J_{0}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}^{p}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
          \approx 9.8\!-\!10.0,
$$

and with the formal domain

$$
J_{m}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
          \approx 9.6\!-\!9.7 .
$$

Hence the textbook gross area between demand and marginal supply up to
$Q^{*}$

$$
W_{g}(Q^{*})=I_{D}(Q^{*})-\int_{Q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
          =CS^{*}+PS_{f}^{*},
$$

with $PS_{f}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-J_{m}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.65\approx11.8\!-\!12.0$,
is

$$
W_{g}^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-J_{m}(Q^{*})\approx32.5-9.9\approx22-23,
$$

e.g. $W_{g}^{*}\approx22.6$ for $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$,
$CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{f}^{*}\approx11.8$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$.

In the economically relevant zero-price normalisation the producer
surplus is measured from $Q_{0}^{p}$,

$$
PS_{e}^{*}=P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}^{p}\right)-J_{0}(Q^{*})
        \approx14.9-9.9\approx5.0\!-\!5.3,
$$

and the net dead-weight free surplus

$$
W_{e}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{e}^{*}
       =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}^{p}-J_{0}(Q^{*})
       \approx32.5-6.7-9.9\approx15\!-\!16\approx15.9,
$$

$CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{e}^{*}\approx5.1$, which is the $W_{e}\approx
15.9$ commonly quoted when the negative-price tail
$Q_{m}<q<Q_{0}^{p}$ is removed.  The $W_{g}\approx22\!-\!23$ value is the
conventional $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-\int_{Q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$ gross total
surplus at the competitive pair $Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.6$.

public_text.13:
The root and the demand side are settled. 

$P_S(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)$ , $P_D(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$,
$P_S(Q^*)=P_D(Q^*)$ gives
$\ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^*}$,
$Q^*\approx4.69\!-\!4.70$, $P^*\approx4.62\!-\!4.63$,
$P^*Q^*\approx21.6\!-\!21.8$,

and
$\int_{0}^{Q^*}P_D(q)dq=18\int_{0}^{Q^*}e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx32.4\!-\!32.8$,
about $32.5$ with the usual Simpson grid. So
$CS=\int_{0}^{Q^*}P_D-P^*Q^*\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!10.9$,
$\approx10.8$ is robust.

The supply side has to be treated economically. $P_S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ is
negative on $2^{1/3}<q<\hat q$ with $\hat q^{3}=3$, i.e.
$q_0=\root3\of3\approx1.442$ is the first zero of the inverse supply,
$P_S(q_0)=0$.  Producer surplus is the area above the marginal cost
curve and below $P^*$ but only where the curve is economically relevant,
$q\ge q_0$.
$P_S(q)<0$ for $2^{1/3}<q<q_0$ is a formal artefact of the log and
should not be counted as a cost saving.

Hence on the admissible non-negative part
$$
PS_{e}=\int_{q_0}^{Q^*}\!\!\big[P^*-P_S(q)\big]dq
     =P^*\!\left(Q^*-q_0\right)-\int_{q_0}^{Q^*}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq .
$$
Numerically
$\int_{q_0}^{Q^*}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8\!-\!10.0$,
$P^*(Q^*-q_0)\approx4.62\,(4.69-1.44)\approx14.9\!-\!15.0$,
so
$PS_{e}\approx14.9-9.9\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$, about $5.1$.

Total dead-weight-free surplus measured from the zero-price origin is
$$
W_e=CS+PS_{e}
   =\int_{0}^{Q^*}P_D(q)dq-P^*q_0-\int_{q_0}^{Q^*}P_S(q)dq
   \approx32.5-4.62\times1.442-9.9\approx15.8\!-\!16.2,
$$
about $15.9$ with the $Q^*\approx4.69$, $P^*\approx4.62$ root quoted
above.

The $ \approx22\!-\!23$ number that is often quoted,
$W_b=\int_{0}^{Q^*}P_Ddq-\int_{q_0}^{Q^*}P_Sdq\approx32.5-9.9\approx22.6$,
is the formal gross area between demand and supply up to $Q^*$.  It is
$CS+PS$ if $PS$ is written as $P^*Q^*-\int_{q_0}^{Q^*}P_S$, i.e. if the
rectangle $P^*q_0$ is kept in the producer surplus.  Economically that
rectangle is not created by trade; once the supply curve is truncated at
its zero-price intercept $q_0= \root3\of3$ the meaningful producer surplus
is $P^*(Q^*-q_0)-\int_{q_0}^{Q^*}P_S$ and the textbook $CS+PS$ is
$\approx10.8+5.1\approx15.9$, the $15\!-\!16$ welfare usually reported
for the $Q^*\approx4.7$, $P^*\approx4.6$ equilibrium. ∎

public_text.5:
I agree with the consensus on the clearing point. 
$P_{s}(Q)=P_{d}(Q)$ is

$\ln(Q^{3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$,

$Q> \sqrt[3]{2}$ and the root is unique. Newton/bisection gives

$Q^{*}\approx4.69\!-\!4.70$, 
$P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.61\!-\!4.63$,

about $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$ and $P^{*}\simeq4.62$.  $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$ is
robust and the consumer surplus

$CS =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*}$, $P_{d}=18e^{-\arctan q}$,

is essentially independent of the supply lower limit. Numerically

$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx 32.4\!-\!32.5$,

so that

$CS\approx 32.4-21.7\approx 10.7\!-\!11.0$,

$\approx 10.8$ with the usual quadrature. That part is solid.

The issue is the producer surplus.  $P_{s}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ is negative
for $\sqrt[3]{2}<q<\sqrt[3]{3}$ and is $0$ at the economic origin

$P_{s}(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}-2=1\iff Q_{0}=\sqrt[3]{3}\approx1.44$.

Marginal cost is not economically meaningful for $q<Q_{0}$; the
region $ \sqrt[3]{2}<q<Q_{0}$ where $P_{s}<0$ is an unphysical negative-cost
tail of the log.  The economically relevant producer surplus is therefore

$PS_{e}= \int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-P_{s}(q)\big]dq
      =P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}
        \ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq$,

and not $P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}$.  With $Q_{0}\approx1.442$,

$\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx 9.8\!-\!10.0$,

$P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})\approx 4.62\,(4.69-1.44)\approx14.9\!-\!15.0$,

hence

$PS_{e}\approx14.98-9.90\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$,

about $5.1$ on the Simpson grid used above.  The usual textbook total
surplus is then

$W_{e}=CS+PS_{e}
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq-P^{*}Q_{0}
      -\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq$,

i.e. the willingness to pay up to $Q^{*}$ minus the variable cost
incurred from the zero-price point onward.  Numerically

$W_{e}\approx 32.45-4.62\times1.442-9.90
   \approx 32.45-6.66-9.90
   \approx 15.9$,

$CS\approx10.8$, $PS_{e}\approx5.1$, $W_{e}\approx15\!-\!16$ monetary
units at $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.

The often quoted $\approx22\!-\!23$ “area between the curves’’
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}dq\approx32.5-9.9\approx
22.6$ is the gross net benefit $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}$
and contains the $P^{*}Q_{0}$ rectangle.  Removing that rectangle, which
is the usual $CS+PS$ definition with $PS$ measured from the zero-price
intercept, gives the economically meaningful total welfare $\approx15.9\approx
16$ at the competitive equilibrium $Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.6$. ∎

public_text.14:
The clearing price is indeed the unique solution of
$\ln(Q^{3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ on $Q>2^{1/3}$.
$F(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$ is monotone increasing and
$F(4.68)<0<F(4.70)$, Newton gives

$Q^{*}\simeq4.69\!-\!4.70$, $t^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\simeq1.36$,
$P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-t^{*}}\simeq4.61\!-\!4.63$, 
say $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$.

With $P_{d}(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$,
$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq$,
$I_{D}(Q^{*})=18\int_{0}^{t^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt\approx 32.4\!-\!32.5$,
so that on the usual definition

$CS= I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!10.9$,
about $10.8$ in the same units.

The inverse marginal cost $P_{s}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ is negative on
$2^{1/3}<q<3^{1/3}$.  The economic origin of supply is $P_{s}=0$,
$P_{s}(q_{0})=0\iff q_{0}^{3}=3$,

$q_{0}=\root3\of{3}\approx1.44$, and $P_{s}(q)\ge0$ for $q\ge q_{0}$.
The economically meaningful producer surplus is therefore

$PS =\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[\,P^{*}-P_{s}(q)\,\big]dq
    =P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-q_{0}\right)-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$.

Numerically
$J(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8\!-\!10.0$,
$P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_{0})\approx4.62\,(4.69-1.44)\approx14.9\!-\!15.0$,
hence

$PS\approx14.98-9.86\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$, about $5.1$.

Hence the dead-weight-free surplus measured from the zero-price
origin is

$W_{e}=CS+PS
      =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_{0}-J(Q^{*})
      \approx32.5-4.62\times1.44-9.9\approx15\!-\!16$,

e.g. $I_{D}\approx32.4$, $P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.65$, $J\approx9.86$ giving
$W_{e}\approx15.9$.  In particular $CS\approx10.8$ and $PS_{e}\approx5.1$
for $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.

The formal “area between the curves’’ 
$W_{b}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-J(Q^{*})\approx32.5-9.9\approx22.6$,
$CS+PS+P^{*}q_{0}$, is often quoted as the gross $P_{d}-P_{s}$ area.
Removing the non-economic $P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.6$ rectangle that arises
from integrating the log supply through its negative-price region
$2^{1/3}<q<3^{1/3}$ leaves the $ \sim15\!-\!16$ net consumer-plus-producer
surplus that is normally used in welfare accounting. ∎

Round 1 synthesis

* Market clearing
  * $P_S(P)=\ln(Q^{3}-2),\;P_D(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$, $Q>2^{1/3}$.
  * $P_S=P_D\iff \ln(Q^{3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$.
  * Unique interior root, monotone LHS up, RHS down.
  * Consensus $Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.70$, stable $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, 
    $t^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36$ rad.
  * $P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.61\!-\!4.63$, consensus $\approx4.62$.
  * $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.6\!-\!21.8$, $\approx21.7$.

* Integrals
  * Demand: $I_D(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx32.4\!-\!32.8$, 
    consensus $\approx32.5$, robust across Simpson/Trapezoid.
  * Supply: $P_S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ first hits zero at $q_0^{p}$ with $P_S=0\iff q_0^{p3}=3$, 
    $q_0^{p}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$. Formal domain start $q_m=2^{1/3}\approx1.260$.
  * $J_0(Q^{*})=\int_{q_0^{p}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8\!-\!10.1$, consensus $\approx9.9$.
  * $J_m(Q^{*})=\int_{q_m}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.6\!-\!9.8$, 
    negative-price tail $\int_{q_m}^{q_0^{p}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx-0.13$ is tiny.

* Surplus splits – persistent disagreement
  * Consumer surplus is stable: $CS=I_D-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0$, consensus $\approx10.8$.
  * Producer surplus definitions split the group:
    * Gross textbook form $PS_g=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_0^{p}}^{Q^{*}}P_S$ 
      $\approx11.8\!-\!12.3$, typical $\approx11.8$.
    * Economic zero-price form $PS_e=\int_{q_0^{p}}^{Q^{*}}[P^{*}-P_S]dq
      =P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_0^{p})-J_0\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$, typical $\approx5.1$.
  * Two welfare numbers are quoted in round 1:
    * Net-benefit / area-between-curves $W_N=I_D-J_0\approx22\!-\!23$, 
      consensus $22.5\!-\!22.6$ with $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.
      This is $W_N=CS+PS_g$ and is what most colleagues report as “total welfare”.
    * Standard CS+PS with zero-price origin $W_e=CS+PS_e=I_D-P^{*}q_0^{p}-J_0
      \approx15\!-\!16$, $\approx15.9$. 
      $W_e=W_N-P^{*}q_0^{p}$ with $P^{*}q_0^{p}\approx6.6$.

* Arguments
  * For $W_N\approx22\!-\!23$: supply is integrated from its economic zero $q_0^{p}=3^{1/3}$,
    producer surplus written as $P^{*}Q^{*}-\int P_S$, consumer surplus as usual.
    This matches the formal expression $\int_0^{Q^{*}}P_D-\int_{q_0^{p}}^{Q^{*}}P_S$.
  * For $W_e\approx15\!-\!16$: $P_S<0$ on $2^{1/3}<q<3^{1/3}$ is non-economic; 
    producer surplus should be $\int_{q_0^{p}}^{Q^{*}}[P^{*}-P_S]dq$,
    removing the $P^{*}q_0^{p}$ rectangle. This is the economically meaningful
    dead-weight free surplus.

* Unresolved / what remains
  * Which lower limit the questioner wants for producer surplus: formal domain $2^{1/3}$ vs economic zero $3^{1/3}$.
  * Numerical quadrature error $\pm0.5$ on $W$ but root $Q^{*},P^{*}$ robust.
  * No closed form for $\int e^{-\arctan q}dq$; all values numeric.

Current best estimate: $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$, $CS\approx10.8$.
Gross area-between-curves total welfare $W_N=I_D-J_0\approx22\!-\!23$, $\approx22.6$, 
which reduces to the conventional zero-price producer-surplus total $W_e\approx15\!-\!16$, 
$\approx15.9$, $PS_e\approx5.1$. The $22\!-\!23$ figure is the number most colleagues quote as total welfare; the $15\!-\!16$ figure is the economically normalised CS+PS.

Market clearing is the unique solution of
$F(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0$, $Q>2^{1/3}$, $F'>0$.
$F(4.68)<0<F(4.70)$ and Newton/bisection gives

* $Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.71$, consensus $Q^{*}\approx4.69\!-\!4.70$, commonly quoted $Q^{*}\approx4.692$,

Demand integral is robust:
$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
      =18\int_{0}^{t^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt\approx32.4\!-\!32.8$, 
commonly $\approx32.45\!-\!32.50$.

Hence
$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0$, consensus $\approx10.8$.

Supply side. The inverse supply $S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ is defined for $q>2^{1/3}\approx1.26$ and $S(q)<0$ on $2^{1/3}<q<3^{1/3}$.
Zero-price intercept
$S(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3$, $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$,
and the formal domain limit $Q_{m}=2^{1/3}\approx1.260$.

$J_{0}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8\!-\!10.1$, consensus $\approx9.86\!-\!9.95$,
$J_{m}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.6\!-\!9.8$.

The $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.6$ rectangle is the difference $W_{g}^{*}-W_{e}^{*}$.

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The clearing point is by now completely settled and I agree with the numbers everyone is quoting.

$P_{S}(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)$, $P_{D}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$,
$F(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0$ is monotone on $Q>2^{1/3}$ and
$F(4.68)<0<F(4.70)$.

* $Q^{*}\approx4.68\!-\!4.70\approx4.69$
* $P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.61\!-\!4.63\approx4.62$
* $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.6\!-\!21.8$

The demand side is also settled.

$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
      =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt\approx32.4\!-\!32.8\approx32.5$

Hence
$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0\approx10.8$
and that part is independent of how the supply integral is written.

The welfare accounting is where the economic meaning matters. 
$P_{S}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ is negative on $2^{1/3}<q<3^{1/3}$ and 
$P_{S}(q_{0})=0\iff q_{0}^{3}=3$, $q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$.
For $2^{1/3}<q<q_{0}$ the log supply is a formal artefact with negative
marginal cost/price. Producer surplus is economically defined only where
marginal cost is non-negative, i.e. from the zero-price origin $q_{0}$.

Put
$J_{0}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8\!-\!10.0\approx9.9$.

The economically relevant producer surplus is
$PS_{e}=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-P_{S}(q)\big]dq
      =P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_{0})-J_{0}(Q^{*})$
$\approx4.62\,(4.69-1.442)-9.9\approx14.99-9.9\approx5.0\!-\!5.3\approx5.1$.

Total dead-weight-free surplus measured from the zero-price origin is then
$W_{e}=CS^{*}+PS_{e}
     =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_{0}-J_{0}(Q^{*})$
$\approx32.5-4.62\times1.442-9.9$
$\approx32.5-6.66-9.9\approx15.8\!-\!16.2\approx15.9$.

So $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{e}\approx5.1$, $W_{e}\approx15\!-\!16$, about
$15.9$ for $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.

The $W_{g}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-J_{0}(Q^{*})\approx32.5-9.9\approx22.6$ figure that is
often quoted as $CS+PS_{g}$ with $PS_{g}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$
is the formal gross area $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$.
It contains the $P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.6$ rectangle and implicitly keeps the
negative-price tail $2^{1/3}<q<3^{1/3}$ in the accounting. Once the supply
curve is truncated at its economic zero $q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ the conventional
$CS+PS$ is the net $W_{e}\approx15.9$, the $\approx22\!-\!23$ number being
$W_{e}+P^{*}q_{0}$.

That is the $Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.6$ equilibrium total welfare
normally reported with the zero-price producer-surplus normalisation.

$$P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\iff

$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq
       =18\int_{0}^{t^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du\approx32.4\!-\!32.8\approx32.5,
$$

$$
CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0\approx10.8,

and it is robust to the supply lower limit.

           =\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq

PS_{e}= \int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\!\big[P^{*}-S(q)\big]dq
      =P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-J_{0}(Q^{*})
      \approx4.62\,(4.69-1.442)-9.9
      \approx14.9-9.9\approx5.0\!-\!5.3\approx5.1 .
$$

W_{e}=CS^{*}+PS_{e}
     =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-J_{0}(Q^{*})
     \approx32.5-4.62\times1.442-9.9
     \approx15\!-\!16\approx15.9,
$$

i.e. $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{e}\approx5.1$, $W_{e}\approx15.9$ at the

$$

$$

$$

        =I_{D}(Q^{*})-J_{0}(Q^{*})
        \approx32.5-9.9\approx22\!-\!23,

e.g. $W_{g}^{*}\approx22.6$ with $Q^{*}=4.69$, $P^{*}=4.62$, $CS^{*}\approx10.8$,

$J_0(Q^{*})=\int_{q_0}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8\!-\!10.0\approx9.86$

be the variable-cost area on the non-negative part of the supply.  The economically relevant producer surplus is measured from the zero-price origin,

$PS_e=\int_{q_0}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-P_S(q)\big]dq
     =P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_0)-J_0(Q^{*}),$

and not $P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_0}^{Q^{*}}P_S$.  Numerically

$P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_0)\approx4.62\,(4.69-1.442)\approx14.9\!-\!15.0,$

$PS_e\approx14.99-9.86\approx5.0\!-\!5.3\approx5.1.$

Hence the dead-weight-free total surplus measured from the zero-price intercept is

$W_e=CS^{*}+PS_e
    =I_D(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_0-J_0(Q^{*})
    \approx32.5-4.62\times1.442-9.86
    \approx32.5-6.66-9.86
    \approx15.8\!-\!16.2\approx15.9,$

with $CS^{*}\approx10.8$ and $PS_e\approx5.1$ at $Q^{*}\approx4.69,\;P^{*}\approx4.62$.

The $\approx22\!-\!23$ number $I_D-J_0\approx32.5-9.9\approx22.6$ is the formal gross area $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_D-\int_{q_0}^{Q^{*}}P_S$, i.e. $CS^{*}+P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_0}^{Q^{*}}P_S$, which retains the $P^{*}q_0\approx6.6$ rectangle and implicitly counts the negative-price tail $2^{1/3}<q<3^{1/3}$ of the log supply.  Once the supply is truncated at its economic zero $q_0=3^{1/3}$ the conventional $CS+PS$ welfare accounting is $W_e\approx15\!-\!16$, about $15.9$ for the $Q^{*}\approx4.7,\;P^{*}\approx4.6$ competitive equilibrium.

$$P_{S}(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right),\qquad

i.e.

$$F(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0 , \qquad F'>0 .$$

$F(4.68)<0<F(4.70)$ and

* $Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.70$, $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,

  $P^{*}\approx4.62$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.6\!-\!21.8$,

is the unique interior competitive pair.  Put $D(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$,
$S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ and $Q_{0}^{p}$ the zero-price intercept of the
inverse supply

$$S(Q_{0}^{p})=0\iff Q_{0}^{p3}=3,\qquad Q_{0}^{p}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442,$$

$Q_{m}=2^{1/3}\approx1.260$ being the formal domain of the log.

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq
       =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq
       =18\int_{0}^{t^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt\approx32.4\!-\!32.8\approx32.5,$$

$$J_{0}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}^{p}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
      =\int_{Q_{0}^{p}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq\approx9.8\!-\!10.0\approx9.9,$$

$J_{m}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq\approx9.6\!-\!9.7$.  On the

$$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0\approx10.8,$$

        \approx21.7-9.9\approx11.8\!-\!12.0 $$

and the formal area between demand and marginal supply up to the
clearing quantity

$$W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}
       =I_{D}(Q^{*})-\int_{Q_{0}^{p}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-\int_{Q_{0}^{p}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
       \approx32.5-9.9\approx22\!-\!23,$$

e.g. with $Q^{*}=4.69$, $P^{*}=4.62$

the usual $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-\int_{Q_{0}^{p}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$ gross

$$W_{g}(Q^{*})= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-
            \int_{Q_{0}^{p}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq,

which is the $W\approx22\!-\!23$ total welfare normally reported.

       =P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}^{p}\right)-J_{0}(Q^{*})
       \approx5.0\!-\!5.3\approx5.1,$$

     =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}^{p}-J_{0}(Q^{*})
     \approx32.5-6.66-9.9\approx15\!-\!16\approx15.9,$$

i.e. $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{e}\approx5.1$, $W_{e}\approx15.9$, the
$P^{*}Q_{0}^{p}\approx6.6$ rectangle being the difference

pair and $CS^{*}\approx10.8$ are invariant under the two normalisations.

The clearing pair is the unique interior solution of

$$P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\iff

$F(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$ is strictly increasing on the
admissible branch and $F(4.68)<0<F(4.70)$.  Bisection/Newton gives

* $Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.70$, $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
* $t^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\simeq1.36\;{\rm rad}$,
* $P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-t^{*}}\simeq4.61\!-\!4.63$,
  $P^{*}\approx4.62$,

$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.6\!-\!21.8\approx21.7$.

Put $D(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and $S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$.  With
$u=\arctan q$

$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq
       =18\int_{0}^{t^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du\approx32.4\!-\!32.8\approx32.5,
$$

so that on the usual inverse definition

$$
CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0\approx10.8,
$$

and it is robust to the supply lower limit.

The inverse supply first hits the price axis at

$$
S(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}-2=1\iff Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442,
$$

and $S(q)<0$ for $2^{1/3}<q<Q_{0}$.  On the economically non-negative
part

$$
J_{0}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
           =\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
           \approx9.8\!-\!10.0\approx9.9 .
$$

Hence the producer surplus measured from the zero-price origin is

$$
PS_{e}= \int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\!\big[P^{*}-S(q)\big]dq
      =P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-J_{0}(Q^{*})
      \approx4.62\,(4.69-1.442)-9.9
      \approx14.9-9.9\approx5.0\!-\!5.3\approx5.1 .
$$

The dead-weight-free market surplus measured from the zero-price
origin is therefore

$$
W_{e}=CS^{*}+PS_{e}
     =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-J_{0}(Q^{*})
     \approx32.5-4.62\times1.442-9.9
     \approx15\!-\!16\approx15.9,
$$

i.e. $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{e}\approx5.1$, $W_{e}\approx15.9$ at the

In the formal textbook gross notation

$$
PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-J_{0}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.9\approx11.8\!-\!12.0,
$$

$$
W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}
        =I_{D}(Q^{*})-J_{0}(Q^{*})
        \approx32.5-9.9\approx22\!-\!23,
$$

e.g. $W_{g}^{*}\approx22.6$ with $Q^{*}=4.69$, $P^{*}=4.62$, $CS^{*}\approx10.8$,

$W_e=CS^*+PS_e=I_D-P^*Q_0-J_0\approx32.5-6.66-9.9\approx15\!-\!16\approx15.9$
$W_e=W_g^*-P^*Q_0$, $P^*Q_0\approx6.6$.

7.text:
The admissible branch is $Q>2^{1/3}$,

$P_{S}(Q)=\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)\uparrow$, 
$P_{D}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}\downarrow$,
$F(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0$,
$F'>0$, $F(4.68)<0<F(4.70)$.

Hence the unique interior clearing pair is

* $Q^{*}\simeq4.68$–$4.70$, $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
* $t^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36$ rad,
* $P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.61$–$4.63$, 
  $P^{*}\approx4.62$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$.

Demand is invariant

$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
      =18\int_{0}^{t^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt\approx32.4\!-\!32.8\approx32.5$,

$$
CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0\approx10.8 .
$$

$P_{S}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)<0$ on $2^{1/3}<q<3^{1/3}$. The first economic zero
of the inverse marginal cost is

$S(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3$, $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$, 
$Q_{m}=2^{1/3}\approx1.260$ the formal log domain.

On the non-negative part

$J_{0}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8\!-\!10.0\approx9.86$.

Measured from the economic zero-price origin the admissible producer
surplus is

$$
PS_{e}= \int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\!\big[P^{*}-S(q)\big]dq
      =P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-J_{0}(Q^{*})
      \approx4.62\,(4.69-1.442)-9.86\approx5.0\!-\!5.3\approx5.1,
$$

and the dead-weight-free total measured from $Q_{0}$

$$
W_{e}=CS^{*}+PS_{e}
     =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-J_{0}(Q^{*})
     \approx32.5-4.62\times1.442-9.86
     \approx15.8\!-\!16.2\approx15.9,
$$

i.e. $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{e}\approx5.1$, $W_{e}\approx15\!-\!16$,
about $15.9$, at $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.

Remark. In the formal textbook $P^{*}Q^{*}$ normalisation

$PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-J_{0}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.9\approx11.8\!-\!12.0$,

$W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-J_{0}(Q^{*})\approx32.5-9.9\approx22\!-\!23$, 
e.g. $W_{g}^{*}\approx22.6$, $PS_{g}^{*}\approx11.8$, for $Q^{*}=4.69$,
$P^{*}=4.62$. $W_{g}^{*}=W_{e}+P^{*}Q_{0}$ with $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.66$,
the $P^{*}Q_{0}$ rectangle removed when producer surplus is defined from
the zero-price intercept $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$. The clearing $Q^{*}\approx4.7$,
$P^{*}\approx4.6$, $CS^{*}\approx10.8$ is common to both conventions.

$W_e=CS^{*}+PS_e
